pluto-prediscovery.caption: Filtered close-ups of the three plates, 2′ square, north up; blue circle: Pluto's predicted position; red cross: the measured image center.
pluto-prediscovery.alt: Three grayscale panels from plates MA 731 (December 21, 1908), B2247a and B2248b (February 20, 1909), each with a dark spot inside a small blue circle at the center.

pentagon-billiard-periods.caption: The six periodic billiard paths in the regular pentagon that are not symmetric under a fifth of a turn, of periods 8, 10, 30, 42, 58 and 102.
pentagon-billiard-periods.alt: Six regular pentagons, each crossed by one blue periodic billiard path, labeled period 8, 10, 30, 42, 58 and 102; the longer the period, the denser the path.

path-ramsey.caption: A 3-coloring of the edges of K17 with no one-colored 10-vertex path, compressed into four parts; edges inside a part have color 0.
path-ramsey.alt: Four circles labeled A: 5, B: 4, C: 4 and D: 4, joined in pairs by red solid, blue dashed and green dotted lines for colors 0, 1 and 2.

thomson-10.caption: The optimal arrangement of ten charges on a sphere, the bicapped square antiprism, from the side and from above (illustration only).
thomson-10.alt: Two views of ten numbered points on a sphere: from the side, two stacked squares with one point above and one below; from above, the lower square turned by 45 degrees.

ekg-bounds.caption: Left: a(n)/n for n ≤ 60 between the sharp bounds 12/7 and 13/28. Right: the largest and smallest a(n)/n in each dyadic block up to 10^6.
ekg-bounds.alt: Two plots. Left: dots for a(n)/n up to n = 60 between lines at 12/7 and 13/28, touching them at n = 7 and 28. Right: block extremes settling near 1.5 and 0.5.

locked-trominoes.caption: A locked tromino tiling of the 15 × 17 rectangle, glued from four blocks of heights 6 and 9 and widths 8 and 9; dashed lines are the seams.
locked-trominoes.alt: A rectangle tiled by L-shaped and straight three-cell tiles in four pastel colors, crossed by one red dashed horizontal and one red dashed vertical line.

steinberg-c4-c9.caption: The 82-vertex planar graph with no 4-cycles or 9-cycles that is not 3-colorable.
steinberg-c4-c9.alt: A planar graph drawn inside a circle: a few vertices on the boundary joined by long edges, with many small clusters of short edges between them.

tight-cycle-c5-turan.caption: The recursive construction giving the lower bound: every triple with two vertices in A and one in B, repeated inside B.
tight-cycle-c5-turan.alt: Two ovals labeled A and B; a blue triangle has two corners in A and one in B, and a smaller oval labeled repeat sits inside B.

game-grundy-gap.caption: The 11-vertex graph used to answer Havet and Zhu's question on the greedy coloring game.
game-grundy-gap.alt: A graph of eleven circled vertices numbered 0 to 10, joined by straight gray edges, some of which cross.

lit-only-sigma.caption: The 7-vertex counterexample to the Goldwasser–Wang–Wu conjecture; blue vertices are lit at the start.
lit-only-sigma.alt: Seven numbered vertices, six on a hexagon around vertex 6, joined by many straight and curved edges; vertices 0, 1, 3 and 4 are blue.

pseudostandard-attractors.caption: The 36-letter binary prefix with the attractor positions 3, 7, 15, 21 and 25 shaded, and the three regions of the lower-bound proof below.
pseudostandard-attractors.alt: A row of 36 boxed binary digits with five boxes shaded blue, and three brackets below marked at least 2, at least 1 and at least 2.

locally-toroidal-polytopes.caption: The facet map {4,4}(3,0) and vertex-figure map {4,4}(9,0) for one instance, as square grids with opposite sides identified.
locally-toroidal-polytopes.alt: Two square grids, 3 by 3 and 9 by 9, each with arrows on opposite sides showing they are glued into a torus and one corner cell shaded.

scattering-coefficients.caption: The rays with a nonzero coefficient in total degree at most 12: blue below the diagonal, red above it, and the diagonal in black.
scattering-coefficients.alt: Rays fanning out from the origin in the positive quadrant: blue rays below the diagonal, red rays above it, and a thick black diagonal.

makonzi-invariants.caption: The three-armed quiver: two vertices joined by three doubled paths, with arrows D and U in each direction.
makonzi-invariants.alt: Two points labeled s and q joined by three pairs of curves, labeled D1 and U1, D2 and U2, U3 and D3.

noncrossing-symmetric-chains.caption: A symmetric chain decomposition of a product of chains of lengths two and three, the kind of partition the paper finds for noncrossing lattices.
noncrossing-symmetric-chains.alt: A 3 by 4 grid of points labeled (i, j), covered by three colored chains: blue for ranks 0 to 5, orange for ranks 1 to 4, green for ranks 2 to 3.

weak-parking.caption: The parking construction in the smallest case, type A2: three reflection lines, Coxeter rotation, and the fiber sizes over each flat.
weak-parking.alt: Three lines through a point with an arrow marking a 120-degree rotation, beside a table of fiber sizes adding up to 16 parking points.

pentagon-tetrads.caption: A holeless tetrad of four congruent hexagons, of the type found by Scott Kim; the paper shows no such tetrad exists for pentagons.
pentagon-tetrads.alt: Four congruent hexagons in orange, green, blue and red, packed so each touches the other three along an edge, with no gap between them.

maximal-matching-logconcavity.caption: The 76-vertex counterexample: six disjoint edges joined to two disjoint cliques of order 32.
maximal-matching-logconcavity.alt: A box of six vertical edges above two circles labeled 32-vertex clique, with thick bars from the box to each circle and none between them.

acyclic-root-extrema.caption: The complement of the 12-vertex counterexample: a four-cycle and two disjoint three-leaf stars.
acyclic-root-extrema.alt: A square of four vertices beside two stars, each a center vertex with three leaves.

zero-forcing-unimodality.caption: The 73-vertex counterexample: cliques of orders 32 and 33, each completely joined to four disjoint edges.
zero-forcing-unimodality.alt: Two circles labeled K32 and K33 on the left and four circles labeled K2 on the right, with a line from each left circle to every right circle.

geneson-continuous-gluing.caption: The common anchor (c,d) and the two allowed quadrants: a pattern P to the southwest and a pattern Q to the northeast.
geneson-continuous-gluing.alt: A point labeled (c,d) at the corner where a blue box of points labeled P to the lower left meets an orange box of points labeled Q to the upper right.

independent-monophonic-ng.caption: The graph H: the complete graph on six vertices with each of its fifteen edges subdivided once.
independent-monophonic-ng.alt: Six black numbered vertices joined by straight lines, each line carrying one small blue vertex at its middle.

spinning-switches.caption: The puzzle: the solver changes hidden switches, then an adversary may swap their positions.
spinning-switches.alt: Two circles marked with question marks, an arrow, then the same two circles with curved arrows swapping them; a note says states and swaps stay hidden.
